#3 The second paragraph of the Idea section has been changed. Their is the (understandable) misconception running throughout nLab probability pages that quantum probability theory is distinct and unrelated to standard probability theory. Thanks to Jacob Barandes we know that is not true. The expectation value functional are the components of the GGG-algebras of the Giry monad which tie everything together. (Well it’s not tied together yet from the category theory perspective but we should work towards that end.)

Added the redirect for the term expected value which I want for a link on the Giry monad page. This page should be the tie that links probability and its applications to probabilistic theories like the theory of quantum mechanics (as a stochastic process).

content:
#5 How about the statement:

Taking the expectation values as the primary concept to develop probability theory (Whittle 92) paves the way to explain quantum mechanics from a (classical) probability viewpoint. The modeling of quantum mechanics as an indivisible stochastic process and using probability theory, developed by Jacob Barandes, explicates the path to achieve this viewpoint.

My issues with your statement are: (1) The statement: Taking the concept of expectation values as the primary … The ‘’primary’’ for what? If you have read Whittle the sentence is meaningful, otherwise it strikes me as an incomplete thought. (2) When you say ‘’quantum probability theory’’ I assume you are referring to the theory that physicist use to EXPLAIN quantum mechanics (computations). That ‘’quantum probability theory’’ is NOT necessary to explain q.m. When I say: ‘’There is the (understandable) misconception running throughout nLab probability pages that quantum probability theory is distinct and unrelated to standard probability theory.’’ this is exactly my point. Quantum probability theory is precisely like the idea of superposition and the wave function… and the mysticism associated with these ancillary concepts. Quantum probability theory was developed due to the (complex) Hilbert space modeling of qm. If you view quantum probability theory as a development (concept) independent of q.m. I would like to know the application which cannot viewed as a stochastic process.

Also, I am going to (re)add the redirect to ‘’expected value’‘.
